newsitem.title: USA: LL&E says Algeria test disappointing.
newsitem.headline: LL&E says Algeria test disappointing.

text.p: Louisiana Land and Exploration Co said the MLNE-1 exploratory well in Algeria's Ghadames Basin confirmed the presence of a hydrocarbon column in the TAG I formation and the possible extension of the BKE/ORD field onto Block 405, but the "initial test results are less than our expectations."

It has a 65 percent interest in the block while Talisman Energy Inc holds the rest. Sonatrach, Algeria's national oil and gas company, has the option to participate in development of commercial discoveries.
LL&E said the MLNE-1 well was drilled to a total depth of 4030 meters (13,222 feet) and found a 51 meter (167 feet) hydrocarbon column.

Without reservoir stimulation, the well tested at rates of 750 barrels of 40.3 degree gravity oil and 225,000 cubic feet of natural gas per day through 27 meters (89 feet) of perforations across three separate members of the TAG sandstone sequence. No water, hydrogen sulfide or carbon dioxide were produced during the test, the company said.
"We are obviously pleased that MLNE-1 confirms the presence of a hydrocarbon column on that portion of Block 405 which is adjacent to recent industry discoveries.

"While initial test results are less than our expectations, we believe that higher rates are achievable with reservoir stimulation. We have already contacted a service company to evaluate methods of improving flow rates from the well," LL&E said.

The company said it is continuing to acquire and interpret additional seismic data in the northeastern portion of Block 405. Locations for future drilling in this portion of the block are being evaluated, based on the results of the seismic data together with information from MLNE-1.

In July, LL&E noted, it tested the MLN-1 well, 26 kilometers (16.1 miles) southwest of MLNE-1, at a rate of 15,850 barrels of oil per day and 61 million cubic feet of natural gas per day. A delineation well, MLN-2, began drilling September 2 about two kilometers (1.2 miles) north-northwest of the MLN-1 well.

In May 1995 the first well on Block 405, MLE-1, was tested at a rate of 1,724 barrels of condensate per day and 43 million cubic feet of natural gas per day. The MLE-1 has been suspended pending commercial assessment. All three discoveries were drilled on separate structural features.

The company said the partnership is also processing and evaluating seismic data on Block 215, which lies 200 kilometers (124 miles) to the west of Block 405, and plans to drill its first exploratory well on that block in 1997.
